meta.name: Open Bracket
meta.tagline: The creator games where the crowd is in the bracket.
meta.calendarLocation: Parade Ground, Governors Island, New York, NY
meta.locationDetail: Parade Ground and Colonels Row, Governors Island. Car-free. Ferry only.

hero.kicker: Two days. One island. Open field.
hero.sub: Day 1: open qualifier heats anyone can enter. Day 2: the top 18 qualifiers join teams captained by six creators for the finals, live on the Parade Ground and on the stream.

about.heading: Don't just watch. Qualify.
paragraphs: Open Bracket is a two-day outdoor games event on Governors Island. On Day 1, anyone 18 or older can enter a qualifier heat and play four quick solo games. The top 3 in each heat make the finals, where they're drafted onto teams captained by the creators you watch.

Day 1 has six heats of up to 50 players, run one at a time so the crowd and the stream can follow every heat. Every heat plays the same four games, so the cut is fair. Each creator hosts one heat, then signs at the merch tent for 30 minutes right after it.

Day 2 is the finals. Six teams of four, each with a creator captain and three qualifiers, play eight team and duo games for placement points. No one is eliminated. Every team plays every game, and the team with the most points wins. The whole day streams on Twitch and YouTube.

schedule.heading: Order of play
schedule.note: Times show in your time zone, with Eastern Time (the island's zone) alongside. Use the switch to flip between them. Competitors pick a heat when they register and check in at least 30 minutes before it, or the spot goes to the standby line. Heats run one at a time. There is no lunch break on Day 1: each competitor plays one heat, and the food trucks on Colonels Row are open all day.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Open Qualifiers
days.summary: Six heats of up to 50 players, one at a time, so every heat gets the whole crowd and the whole stream. Every heat plays the same four solo games. The host creator opens with an exhibition round of Paper Ball Shootout, then everyone plays for placement points, and the host announces the top 3. Top 3 in each heat advance: 18 qualifiers.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Finals
days.summary: Six teams of four: one creator captain and three qualifiers, picked in a live draft. Eight team and duo games in three blocks, then the Chat Decides finale. No one is eliminated. Every team plays every game.

games.heading: The games
games.intro: Twelve games. Every Day 1 heat plays the same four solo games. The Day 2 finals have eight team and duo games, and every team plays all of them.

items.name: Paper Ball Shootout
items.desc: Crumple paper and shoot it into trash cans at three distances. Farther cans score more, and no athletic skill is needed.

items.name: Musical Chairs
items.desc: The classic, at full size on the grass. A chair comes out every round until one player is left in each group.

items.name: Sack Sprint
items.desc: Step into a burlap sack and jump 30 meters to the line. Falling is allowed.

items.name: Simon Says
items.desc: One host, one mic, the whole heat. Move without "Simon says" and you're out.

items.name: Skills Challenge
items.desc: A team relay based on an All-Star skills course. Dribble through cones, chest pass to a target, make a layup, then tag the next teammate.

items.name: Crate Stack
items.desc: One climber in a harness, on a staff-run belay, stands on the stack while three teammates hand up crates. Height at the buzzer counts.

items.name: Shuttle Relay
items.desc: Four legs, one baton, cones at each end. Drop the baton and you restart your leg.

items.name: Chat Decides
items.desc: The finale and worth double points. Stream chat votes the obstacle route at every fork.

items.name: Balloon Toss
items.desc: Toss a water balloon to your partner and step back after every catch. Last pair with an unbroken balloon wins.

items.name: Three-Legged Race
items.desc: Ankles tied, 40 meters, one pair per lane.

items.name: Blind Maze
items.desc: One partner is blindfolded. The other guides them through a cone maze by voice only.

items.name: Lag Spike
items.desc: Partners race side by side. When the host calls "lag", both have to move in slow motion until it clears.

games.duoRule: Each duo game takes one pair from every team. Every player plays exactly 2 of the 4 duo games, with a different partner each time, so no team can keep sending its best player.

creators.heading: Creator lineup
creators.intro: Six invited creators. Each one hosts a Day 1 heat, then captains a Day 2 team of three qualifiers. All names below are fictional.

items.name: Rosa Asante
items.bio: Holds records in three retro platformers and streams practice runs at 6 AM.

items.name: Theo Lindqvist
items.bio: Tries a new sport every week and posts every failed attempt.

items.name: Kwame Mori
items.bio: Hosts a nightly party game stream where chat sets the house rules.

items.name: June Marchetti
items.bio: Posts one trick shot a day and shows all the misses before it.

items.name: Luis Park
items.bio: Turns playground games into full tournaments with brackets and commentary.

items.name: Hana Ferreira
items.bio: Variety streamer known for co-op chaos and skipping every tutorial.

creators.more: Meet-and-greets are on Day 1 only: each creator signs at the merch tent for 30 minutes right after the heat they host, one creator at a time. Day 2 has no meet-and-greet.

logistics.heading: Getting there
logistics.intro: Governors Island has no cars and no bridge. The only way on or off is by ferry, from Lower Manhattan, Brooklyn Bridge Park, or Red Hook. The island is open 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM in the fall. NYC Ferry also stops at the island from Manhattan and the Brooklyn waterfront, but it's run separately, so buy those tickets and check those times at ferry.nyc.

steps.label: Departs from
steps.text: Battery Maritime Building, 10 South St, Lower Manhattan.

steps.label: Getting there
steps.text: 1 to South Ferry, R/W to Whitehall St, or 4/5 to Bowling Green. About a 5 minute walk.

steps.label: Fare
steps.text: Free on weekends for any boat before {{t:2026-10-17T11:00:00-04:00}}, through the {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}} boat. From {{t:2026-10-17T11:00:00-04:00}}, $5 round trip for adults. Always free for kids 12 and under, older adults, NYCHA residents, IDNYC holders, military service members, and Governors Island members.

steps.label: Departs from
steps.text: Pier 6, Brooklyn Bridge Park, at the end of Atlantic Ave.

steps.label: Getting there
steps.text: 2/3/4/5 to Borough Hall or R to Court St, then about a 20 minute walk down Atlantic Ave to the water.

steps.label: Days and frequency
steps.text: Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays through Sun, Nov 1, 2026. Hourly from {{t:2026-10-17T10:15:00-04:00}}.

steps.label: Fare
steps.text: The {{t:2026-10-17T10:15:00-04:00}} boat is free on weekends. After that, $5 round trip for adults. Always free for kids 12 and under, older adults, NYCHA residents, IDNYC holders, military service members, and Governors Island members.

steps.label: Departs from
steps.text: Atlantic Basin, Pioneer St and Conover St, Red Hook.

steps.label: Getting there
steps.text: There is no subway nearby. Take the B61 bus to Van Brunt St and Pioneer St, then walk about 2 minutes to the gate at Pioneer and Conover. Walking from the nearest subway (F/G at Smith-9th Sts or Carroll St) takes about 25 to 30 minutes. NYC Ferry's South Brooklyn route also stops at Atlantic Basin.

steps.label: Days and frequency
steps.text: Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays through Sun, Nov 1, 2026. Hourly from {{t:2026-10-17T09:45:00-04:00}}.

steps.label: Fare
steps.text: The {{t:2026-10-17T09:45:00-04:00}} and {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}} boats are free on weekends. After that, $5 round trip for adults. Always free for kids 12 and under, older adults, NYCHA residents, IDNYC holders, military service members, and Governors Island members.

logistics.lastFerryWarning: The island closes at {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}}. Last boats back: {{t:2026-10-17T17:30:00-04:00}} to Red Hook, and {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}} to Brooklyn Bridge Park and to Manhattan. Both days end by {{t:2026-10-17T16:30:00-04:00}}. If you miss the last boat, there is no other way off the island.

cards.title: Check-in on arrival
cards.body: From any landing, follow the Open Bracket signs to the check-in tent on the Parade Ground, about 5 minutes on foot. Show the QR code from your confirmation email to get your wristband. Competitors check in at least 30 minutes before their heat (by {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}} for Heat 1), or the spot goes to the standby line. Spectators get a wristband at the same tent.

cards.title: What to bring
cards.body: Shoes you can run in. Layers and a windproof jacket, because mid-October on the water is cold, especially on the ferry home. A change of socks and a spare shirt for Balloon Toss. Sunscreen. An empty water bottle to refill. A charged phone with your QR code.

cards.title: Water and shade
cards.body: Free water refill stations at every game field and at the main stage. Bring a refillable bottle. Shade tents and seating along Colonels Row. The medical tent is next to check-in.

cards.title: Bag policy
cards.body: Clear bags only, up to 12 x 6 x 12 in, or a one-gallon clear plastic bag. You can also bring one small clutch or fanny pack up to 4.5 x 6.5 in. Empty clear or reusable water bottles are welcome, and you can fill them at any refill station. Every bag is searched and everyone goes through a metal detector at the check-in tent. No glass, coolers, alcohol, or drones, and no bag storage on site.

cards.title: Accessibility
cards.body: The ferries and the event site are wheelchair accessible, and the paths on this part of the island are flat. There is an accessible viewing area at the main stage. Tell us what you need on the registration form.

cards.title: Getting around
cards.body: There are no cars, taxis, or rideshare on the island. The event site is a short walk from the ferry landings. You can bring a bike on the ferry or rent one on the island.

watch.heading: Watch from anywhere
watch.intro: Both days stream live on Twitch and YouTube. Stream times below are in your time zone, with Eastern Time alongside. Add a stream to your calendar so you don't miss the start.

channels.name: Qualifier stream
channels.detail: Every heat, one at a time, with commentary, plus the bracket reveal at {{t:2026-10-17T16:15:00-04:00}}.

channels.name: Finals stream
channels.detail: The team draft, all three blocks, the Chat Decides finale, and awards.

channels.name: Replays
channels.detail: Full replays and clips of each game go up on YouTube within 24 hours of each day.

watch.vote: Stream chat votes the Chat Decides route in the finale, which is worth double points.

registration.heading: Register
registration.intro: Two ways in. Compete to play a Day 1 qualifier heat, with Day 2 entry included. Spectate to watch either day or both.
registration.demoNotice: Demo form. Nothing is sent anywhere and no emails go out. Your registration is saved only in this browser (localStorage).

types.label: Compete
types.desc: Play one Day 1 qualifier heat of four solo games. Top 3 in each heat play the Day 2 finals. Includes Day 2 entry. Ages 18 and up.

types.label: Spectate
types.desc: Watch the heats, the finals, or both from the Parade Ground. All ages. Includes a $5 food truck voucher, so it pays for itself.

items.q: Do I need to be good at games to compete?
items.a: No. The games are simple and short, and most people have never played them in a competition before. Nobody gets to practice ahead of time.

items.q: How do I get to Day 2?
items.a: Finish in the top 3 of your heat. That makes 18 qualifiers in total. They're announced at the Day 1 bracket reveal, {{t:2026-10-17T16:15:00-04:00}}. On Day 2, check in at the green tent by {{t:2026-10-18T10:45:00-04:00}}.

items.q: Can I choose my heat time?
items.a: Yes. You pick one of the six heats when you register. Heats run one at a time, every 45 minutes from {{t:2026-10-17T11:15:00-04:00}} to {{t:2026-10-17T15:45:00-04:00}}. You can switch heats later with the change my registration link while the new heat has room.

items.q: I'm coming from Brooklyn. Can I make the first heat?
items.a: Yes, and the ride is free. The first boat from Red Hook leaves at {{t:2026-10-17T09:45:00-04:00}}, and the first boat from Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 6 leaves at {{t:2026-10-17T10:15:00-04:00}}. Check-in for Heat 1 stays open until {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}}, which leaves time for the crossing and the 5 minute walk to the check-in tent. The Pier 6 boat has less slack, so if you'd rather not cut it close, take the Red Hook or Manhattan ferry, or pick a later heat.

items.q: What if my heat is full?
items.a: Each heat closes at 50 competitors. Pick another heat, or buy a spectator ticket and join the standby line at the check-in tent on the day. Spots from competitors who don't check in go to standby first come, first served, at no extra cost.

items.q: What happens if I miss check-in for my heat?
items.a: Check in at least 30 minutes before your heat, which is {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}} for Heat 1. After that, your spot goes to the standby line and your ticket isn't refunded. You can still watch, and you can join standby for a later heat.

items.q: Can I compete with friends?
items.a: On Day 1, everyone plays solo, but you and your friends can register for the same heat and play side by side. Day 2 teams are drafted live by the creators, so you can't pick your teammates.

items.q: How are points scored?
items.a: Every game awards placement points. On Day 1, each game ranks everyone in your heat and your points add up across the four games. The top 3 totals in each heat advance. If players are tied for a qualifying spot, they settle it head to head on the main stage: 30 seconds of Paper Ball Shootout, most makes wins, and if it's still tied they go again. On Day 2, each game pays 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, and 1 points by team placement. Chat Decides is the last game and pays double. The highest total wins.

items.q: Do creators play on Day 1?
items.a: Each creator hosts one heat. They open it, play an exhibition round of Paper Ball Shootout that doesn't count, and announce the heat's top 3. They compete on Day 2 as team captains.

items.q: When and where is the meet-and-greet?
items.a: Day 1 only, at the merch tent, for 30 minutes right after each creator's heat, one creator at a time: Rosa Asante at {{t:2026-10-17T12:00:00-04:00}}, Theo Lindqvist at {{t:2026-10-17T12:45:00-04:00}}, Kwame Mori at {{t:2026-10-17T13:30:00-04:00}}, June Marchetti at {{t:2026-10-17T14:15:00-04:00}}, Luis Park at {{t:2026-10-17T15:00:00-04:00}}, and Hana Ferreira at {{t:2026-10-17T15:45:00-04:00}}. There is no meet-and-greet on Day 2.

items.q: Is Crate Stack safe?
items.a: Yes. The climber wears a harness clipped to a belay rope run by trained staff, so if the stack falls, the climber doesn't. Climbers must weigh under 250 lb, well inside what standard climbing belay gear is rated for, and staff check every harness before each climb. Anyone who'd rather not climb can pass crates instead.

items.q: Will I be on the stream?
items.a: If you compete, yes. Every heat and every finals game is filmed and streamed. Spectators may also appear in crowd shots. Registering as a competitor means you agree to be filmed.

items.q: Can I watch the stream while I'm on the island?
items.a: Yes. The stream plays on the screen at the main stage all day, and you can open it on your phone. Mobile data can be slow when the crowd is big, so the main stage screen is the reliable option.

items.q: Is there food, and can I bring my own?
items.a: Yes to both. Food trucks on Colonels Row are open all day on both days, and spectator tickets include a $5 voucher. You can bring your own food in your clear bag. Coolers and glass aren't allowed. Refill your water bottle at any refill station.

items.q: What happens if it rains?
items.a: Light rain, we keep playing. Lightning or strong wind, we pause and post updates on this page and by text. If a day is cancelled, every ticket for that day is refunded in full.

items.q: What if it's cold or windy?
items.a: Mid-October on the water is often cool and windy, and the ferry is colder than the island. Bring layers and a windproof jacket. Strong wind can pause Crate Stack and Balloon Toss, and we'll run them later in the block. Lightning or dangerous wind pauses everything, with updates on this page and by text.

items.q: Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
items.a: Yes, a full refund until Fri, Oct 2, 2026. From Sat, Oct 3, 2026, two weeks before the event, tickets are non-refundable. You can still switch to a different heat with the change my registration link while that heat has room.

items.q: Is the ferry included in my ticket?
items.a: No, but on weekends every boat before {{t:2026-10-17T11:00:00-04:00}} is free, from any stop: Manhattan through the {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}} boat, Red Hook at {{t:2026-10-17T09:45:00-04:00}} and {{t:2026-10-17T10:45:00-04:00}}, and Brooklyn Bridge Park at {{t:2026-10-17T10:15:00-04:00}}. After that, it's $5 round trip for adults. Kids 12 and under, older adults, NYCHA residents, IDNYC holders, military service members, and Governors Island members always ride free. Check the island ferry schedule on govisland.com for current fares.

items.q: What if I miss the last ferry?
items.a: There is no other way off the island. The earliest last boat is {{t:2026-10-17T17:30:00-04:00}} to Red Hook, and the last boats to Brooklyn Bridge Park and Manhattan leave at {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}}. Both days end by {{t:2026-10-17T16:30:00-04:00}}, so you have at least an hour.

items.q: Can I bring friends who aren't competing?
items.a: Yes. Spectator tickets are $5, open to all ages, and come with a $5 food truck voucher. Competitors have to be 18 or older.
